bull.b: The sharp FY2026 recovery demonstrates substantial operating leverage when NAND demand and pricing improve. Revenue scale, expanded margins, and the return to significant profitability strengthen internal funding capacity, although the durability of this earnings level depends on sustaining favorable industry conditions.

Long-duration NBMs provide greater revenue visibility than spot-market sales and deepen strategic relationships with Datacenter and Edge customers. Their increasing share of bits can support product planning, capacity decisions, and cash generation across multiple years, while financial guarantees add contractual protection.

A growing Datacenter mix moves the portfolio toward a faster-growing, strategically important end market and reduces reliance on traditional removable media. BiCS 8, QLC, and the announced BiCS 10 roadmap also support higher density, performance, and power efficiency in emerging workloads.

bear.b: The recent turnaround is not yet proven through a full industry cycle because prior years included sizable losses and negative free cash flow. NAND pricing, demand, and margins can therefore reverse sharply, making current earnings and cash generation less dependable for long-term planning.

Weakness in consumer markets can pressure volumes and product mix while PC and smartphone customers adjust. Management’s expectation of recovery only in calendar 2027 indicates that this end-market softness may persist over the next several quarters and could offset strength elsewhere.

NBMs improve visibility but also concentrate more revenue and strategic dependence among a limited number of major customers. Changes in those customers’ requirements, purchasing plans, or financial condition could have an outsized effect on SanDisk’s growth and capacity utilization despite contractual guarantees.
